---
name: slack-api
description: Send, read, search, and manage Slack messages, channels, threads, users, and reactions through the Slack Web API. Use whenever the user asks to post or schedule a message to Slack, reply in a thread, list or create or join channels, read conversation history, search messages, look up users by ID or email, add or remove reactions, or automate any other Slack workspace action with a bot or user token.
---

# Slack API

## Overview

Perform Slack Web API operations (messaging, channels, threads, users, search, reactions) through `scripts/slack_api.cjs`, a zero-dependency Node.js >= 18 client. No SDK installation or Slack-specific tooling is required.

## Authentication

- Provide a token with `--token <token>`, `--token-file <path>`, or the environment variables `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` / `SLACK_TOKEN` (checked in that order).
- Prefer a bot token (`xoxb-...`) for automation. User tokens (`xoxp-...`) act on a person's behalf.
- Required OAuth scopes depend on the operation. The Slack error `missing_scope` names exactly what is needed (e.g. `needed: chat:write`). See the scope table in `references/api-reference.md` before asking a user for a new token.
- Never hardcode tokens, save them in committed files, or echo them in output or summaries. If no token is configured, ask the user for one.

## Quick start

```bash
# Verify the token works
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs auth-test

# Send a message; channels accept an ID (C123ABC) or a name (#general)
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs post "#general" "Hello from automation"

# Read the latest messages in a channel
SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... node scripts/slack_api.cjs history C123ABC --limit 10
```

Run `node scripts/slack_api.cjs help` for the complete command list. Scripts live in this skill's `scripts/` directory; run them from anywhere by referencing the skill path (e.g. `node <skill-dir>/scripts/slack_api.cjs ...`).

## Core operations

### Send and edit messages
- `post <channel> <text...>` — send a message (`chat.postMessage`). Supports `--thread-ts <ts>` to start/continue a thread and `--blocks <json-or-@file>` to send a Block Kit payload (text may be omitted when blocks are used).
- `reply <channel> <thread-ts> <text...>` — reply inside an existing thread.
- `update <channel> <ts> <text...>` — edit a message you posted.
- `delete <channel> <ts>` — delete a message.
- Message content supports Slack mrkdwn formatting (`*bold*`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, `<https://...|link text>`).

### Read messages and activity
- `history <channel> [--limit N] [--cursor C]` — fetch recent messages (`conversations.history`).
- `replies <channel> <ts>` — fetch all replies in a thread.
- `search <query...>` — search messages across the workspace (`search.messages`).
- List endpoints print a `NOTE:` line with `--cursor` when more pages exist; follow it to paginate.

### Channels and users
- `channels`, `channel-info`, `channel-create`, `channel-join`, `channel-leave`, `channel-set-topic`, `users`, `user-info`, `user-by-email` — see `help` for exact arguments.

### Reactions and misc
- `react <channel> <emoji> <ts>` / `unreact ...` — emoji may be written with or without colons (`:+1:` or `+1`).
- `api <method> <json-or-@file>` — call any Web API method directly when no subcommand fits (e.g. `files.upload`, `chat.scheduleMessage`).

## Workflows

### Post a message to a channel given by name
The client resolves `#name` or `name` to a channel ID automatically (searching public and private channels plus DMs). `post "#general" "text"` just works; an ambiguous name yields the candidates instead.

### Summarize recent activity in a channel
1. `history <channel> --limit 30` to fetch recent messages.
2. Read the returned `messages[]` (each has `user`, `text`, `ts`).
3. Summarize the content for the user; post the summary only if asked.

### Reply inside a thread
Take the parent message's `ts` (e.g. `1699999999.000100`) from a `history` or `post` result and call `reply <channel> <ts> "text"`.

### Handle "not_in_channel"
If posting fails with `not_in_channel`, the bot must join first: `channel-join <channel>`, then retry. Private channels require the app to have been added by a member.

## Safety rules

- Only send messages the user explicitly asked to send; do not invent or paraphrase content beyond light, clearly stated cleanup.
- `delete`, `unreact`, and `channel-leave` are destructive: only run them when the user explicitly requests it, and confirm the exact channel + `ts` first.
- Do not dump raw tokens or full token strings anywhere.

## Output conventions

- Success: a `Success: <method>` line followed by the Slack API response as JSON (IDs like `channel`/`ts`, plus `response_metadata.next_cursor` for paging).
- Failure: a single `Failure: ...` line on stderr with a non-zero exit code. Slack error names (`invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, `rate_limited`, ...) are preserved in the message.
- HTTP 429 and 5xx responses are retried automatically with backoff.

## Reference

Read `references/api-reference.md` when you need endpoint details, parameter tables, OAuth scope requirements, or troubleshooting guidance.

# Slack Web API Reference

Companion reference for the `slack-api` skill. Read this file when you need endpoint details, OAuth scope requirements, or troubleshooting guidance. The helper script `scripts/slack_api.cjs` implements the common operations; use its `api <method> <json>` escape hatch for anything not listed here.

## Contents

1. [Conventions](#conventions)
2. [Authentication and scopes](#authentication-and-scopes)
3. [Endpoints by category](#endpoints-by-category)
4. [Pagination](#pagination)
5. [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
6. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Conventions

- **Base URL**: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`. The script POSTs JSON with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Channel IDs** start with `C` (public channel), `G` (private channel or group DM), `D` (DM). **User IDs** start with `U`, bot IDs with `B`. Prefer IDs in API calls; the script resolves names to IDs when given `#name`.
- **Message timestamps (`ts`)** look like `1699999999.000100`. They are opaque identifiers, not dates: always keep them as strings and never convert to numbers. The `ts` of a parent message also identifies its thread and is passed as `thread_ts` when replying.
- **Text formatting**: messages use Slack mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, `` ```pre``` ``, `<https://example.com|Link text>`, `<!channel>`, `<@U123>`. Newlines are fine inside the text field.
- **Block Kit**: `chat.postMessage` etc. accept a `blocks` JSON array for rich layouts (headers, sections, buttons, inputs). When sending blocks you can omit `text`, but note some surfaces (e.g. notifications) fall back to `text` if provided, so include a short text fallback for important messages.

## Authentication and scopes

Tokens never expire by themselves but can be revoked. Ask for a token with the minimal scope set for the task. Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. OAuth **scopes are per workspace installation**; a bot may have different scopes in different workspaces.

| Operation | Web API method | Typical required scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verify token | `auth.test` | none |
| Send / edit / delete messages | `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `chat.delete`, `chat.scheduleMessage` | `chat:write` |
| Read public channel history | `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies` | `channels:history` |
| Read private / group DM / DM history | `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies` | `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| List / inspect channels | `conversations.list`, `conversations.info` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Create channels | `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` (public), `groups:write` (private) |
| Join channels | `conversations.join` | `channels:join` |
| Leave / rename / set topic | `conversations.leave`, `conversations.rename`, `conversations.setTopic`, `conversations.setPurpose` | `channels:manage`, `groups:write` |
| List / look up users | `users.list`, `users.info`, `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read` |
| Search messages | `search.messages` | `search:read` |
| Reactions | `reactions.add`, `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` |
| Upload files | `files.upload` | `files:write` |

When a token is missing a scope, Slack responds `{ "ok": false, "error": "missing_scope", "needed": "chat:write" }` — the `needed` field names the scope to request. The script surfaces it verbatim.

## Endpoints by category

### Messaging
- `chat.postMessage` — body: `{ "channel": "C123", "text": "...", "thread_ts": "optional" }`. Returns `{ "ok": true, "channel": "C123", "ts": "1699999999.000100", "message": {...} }`. The returned `ts` is needed to later update, delete, or react to the message.
- `chat.update` — `{ "channel", "ts", "text" }`; only messages posted by the same bot/user can be edited.
- `chat.delete` — `{ "channel", "ts" }`.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` — like `postMessage` plus `post_at` (Unix time); returns a `scheduled_message_id`. Messages cannot be scheduled more than 120 days out.
- Threads: any message with `thread_ts` set becomes part of the thread of the message with that `ts`. Replies carry a `parent_user_id` and `thread_ts` in responses.

### Conversation content
- `conversations.history` — `{ "channel", "limit", "cursor", "oldest", "latest", "inclusive" }`. `limit` default 100, max 999. `oldest`/`latest` accept Unix timestamps (seconds) or `ts` values; results are newest-first. Messages appear with `user` (author ID), `text`, `ts`, optional `thread_ts`, `reactions`, `files`.
- `conversations.replies` — `{ "channel", "ts" }` fetches the parent message plus all replies in its thread.
- `conversations.list` — `{ "types": "public_channel", "limit": 200, "cursor" }`. `types` is a comma-separated mix of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`. Set `exclude_archived: true` to skip archived channels.
- `conversations.info` — returns channel metadata: `name`, `topic`, `purpose`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`.

### Users
- `users.list` — paginated list; `limit` max 200. Each entry has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `profile.display_name`, `is_bot`, `deleted`.
- `users.info` — `{ "user": "U123" }`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — `{ "email" }`; errors with `users_not_found` when no match.

### Search
- `search.messages` — `{ "query", "count" }`. Query syntax: `from:@alice`, `in:#general`, `after:2024-01-01`, quoted phrases, `is:thread`. Response contains `messages.matches[]` with `channel`/`permalink` context plus paging in `paging`.

### Reactions
- `reactions.add` — `{ "channel", "name": "+1", "timestamp": "1699999999.000100" }`. Emoji names are written without colons (`:+1:` -> `+1`, `:white_check_mark:` -> `white_check_mark`). Custom emoji work by name too.
- `reactions.remove` — same body; errors with `no_reaction` if the emoji is not present.

## Pagination

List and search endpoints paginate with cursors, not offsets:

1. Call with an optional `limit` (e.g. 100).
2. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the result. An empty string means the end.
3. Re-issue the request with `cursor: <next_cursor>` to get the next page.

The script prints a `NOTE: ... --cursor <cursor>` line whenever a next page exists, so follow it iteratively to collect complete results (e.g. a full channel export or full user list).

## Rate limits

Slack rate limits apply per method and are tiered by workspace plan; a typical default is roughly 1 request per second per method, with much higher burst limits on paid plans.

- HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds). The script waits and retries automatically (up to 4 attempts).
- Common causes: tight loops over the same method, or hammering pagination without delay. When iterating pages, respect the response pacing: if you receive a 429, back off at least as long as `Retry-After`.
- Writes (post/update/delete/react) are far less tolerant of bursts than reads. Batch messages with a small delay between sends (e.g. 1s) if posting many at once.

## Troubleshooting

| Slack error | Meaning and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is wrong or revoked. Ask the user for a valid token. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a permission; `needed` lists it. Ask the user to install the app with that scope (see table above). |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must join the channel first: run `channel-join <channel>` (or have an admin add it). |
| `channel_not_found` | ID/name is wrong, or the bot cannot see the channel (not a member / not shared). |
| `is_archived` | The channel is archived; it cannot receive messages. |
| `restricted_action` / `enterprise_is_restricted` | Workspace policy blocks the action for this app/user. |
| `invalid_blocks` | The `blocks` JSON does not conform to Block Kit schema. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds 40,000 characters; split the message. |
| `ratelimited` | Slow down; retry after the delay. |
| `user_not_found` / `users_not_found` | Bad user ID or email. |

General debugging pattern: run `auth-test` first to confirm the token, then the failing call again with `--verbose` to see the raw Slack response, then consult the table.

---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API from Gemini CLI. Use when the user wants to send or update Slack messages (chat.postMessage, chat.update, chat.delete), read channel or DM history (conversations.history), list channels or users, post ephemeral messages, add reactions, look up users by email, paginate through results, or troubleshoot Slack API errors and rate limits.
---

# Slack API Interaction

## Quick start

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api`
- Authenticate every request with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- Read the token from an environment variable such as `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`; never hardcode or print tokens.
- Send JSON with `Content-Type: application/json` unless an endpoint specifies `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
- Every response is an envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}`. Always check `ok` before using payload fields; on failure report the `error` code (and `response_metadata` if present) to the user.

Minimal send example:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C0123456789", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}'
```

## Message sending and lifecycle

- `chat.postMessage`: send a message. Required: `channel` (channel ID, DM ID, or user ID) and either `text` or `blocks`. Optional useful fields: `thread_ts` (reply in a thread), `reply_broadcast`, `mrkdwn`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `link_names`.
- `chat.postEphemeral`: send a message visible only to one `user` in a `channel`.
- `chat.update`: edit a message by `channel` + `ts`.
- `chat.delete`: delete a message by `channel` + `ts`.
- `chat.getPermalink`: get a permanent link for `channel` + `message_ts`.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` / `chat.deleteScheduledMessage`: schedule or cancel a message with a `post_at` Unix timestamp.
- Rich messages: prefer `blocks` (Block Kit JSON) over long `text`. Render user and channel mentions with `<@USERID>` / `<#CHANNELID>`; these are not resolved from display names.
- Returned `ts` values are message IDs and thread timestamps; treat them as opaque strings.

## Conversation and history lookups

Channels, private channels, DMs, and group DMs are all "conversations". Use the `conversations.*` methods:

- `conversations.list`: list conversations. Filter with `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` (comma-separated) and `exclude_archived=true`. Use the returned `id` as the `channel` value.
- `conversations.history`: fetch recent messages. Params: `channel`, `limit` (1–200, default 100), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps), `inclusive`, `include_all_metadata`. Returns newest-first messages in `messages[]`.
- `conversations.replies`: get the full thread (`thread_ts` = parent message `ts`) for a message.
- `conversations.info`: get conversation metadata including `is_archived`, `is_private`, `name`, and `last_read`-style markers.
- `conversations.members`: list member user IDs of a conversation (may require `cursor` pagination).
- To find a DM id for a user, use `conversations.open` with `users=<USERID>` (do not hardcode DM ids, they change).
- `conversations.join` / `conversations.leave` / `conversations.archive` for channel membership operations.

## Users

- `users.list`: list workspace users. May return only the first page with `response_metadata.next_cursor`; paginate when present.
- `users.info`: profile by `user` id. Useful fields: `user.real_name`, `user.profile.display_name`, `user.profile.email`, `user.deleted`, `user.is_bot`.
- `users.lookupByEmail`: resolve a user from an email address.
- `users.conversations`: list conversations a user is in (auth token's user) — useful for enumerating accessible channels.

## Reactions, search, files, pins

- `reactions.add`: `{channel, name, timestamp}`. `reactions.remove` removes one; `reactions.get` reads them.
- Search (`search.messages`, `search.files`) requires a user token with `search:read`; bot tokens generally cannot search. When a search call fails with `missing_scope`, explain the token limitation rather than retrying.
- File upload (modern flow): `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename` and `length`, then POST the file bytes to the returned `upload_url`, then `files.completeUploadExternal` with the returned `file_id`; optionally pass `channel_id` to share. Legacy `files.upload` still works but is deprecated.
- `pins.add` / `pins.list`: pin or list pinned items in a channel.

## Pagination and rate limits

- Pagination: list-style endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Repeat the request adding `cursor=<next_cursor>` until it is empty. Prefer `cursor` over `page`/`count`.
- Rate limits: HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Sleep that long and retry; also honor `X-Slack-Rate-Limit-*` headers and default tier limits by backing off after bursts. For interactive use, space bulk calls out.
- Other common errors to surface: `not_in_channel` (join first), `channel_not_found` (verify the id is a conversation id, not a display name), `invalid_auth` (bad or expired token), `missing_scope` (token lacks a required scope), `is_archived` (channel archived), `ratelimited`.
- Channel/user ids are fixed-prefixed (`C` channels, `D` DMs, `U` users, `W` bot users, `T` teams). Never guess an id; always resolve via the API when unsure.

## Workflow guidance

- Resolve ids before acting: given a channel name or user name/email, first call `conversations.list`/`users.lookupByEmail` to obtain the id, then perform the intended operation.
- Prefer read-only operations when the user asks to inspect; only send, edit, or delete messages when the user clearly requests it. Confirm destructive actions (deletes, message edits) before executing.
- Verify writes: after `chat.postMessage`, surface the returned `ts` and, when asked to confirm delivery, optionally call `conversations.history` to verify.
- Never echo full message bodies of private channels or user tokens into output without need; return trimmed summaries.
- When the Slack API returns a structured error, report `error` plus any `needed`/`provided` scope fields so the user can fix token scopes.

- `api <method> <json-or-@file>` — call any Web API method directly when no subcommand fits (e.g. `files.upload`, `chat.scheduleMessage`).

## Workflows

### Post a message to a channel given by name
The client resolves `#name` or `name` to a channel ID automatically (searching public and private channels plus DMs). `post "#general" "text"` just works; an ambiguous name yields the candidates instead.

### Summarize recent activity in a channel
1. `history <channel> --limit 30` to fetch recent messages.
2. Read the returned `messages[]` (each has `user`, `text`, `ts`).
3. Summarize the content for the user; post the summary only if asked.

### Reply inside a thread
Take the parent message's `ts` (e.g. `1699999999.000100`) from a `history` or `post` result and call `reply <channel> <ts> "text"`.

### Handle "not_in_channel"
If posting fails with `not_in_channel`, the bot must join first: `channel-join <channel>`, then retry. Private channels require the app to have been added by a member.

## Safety rules

- Only send messages the user explicitly asked to send; do not invent or paraphrase content beyond light, clearly stated cleanup.
- `delete`, `unreact`, and `channel-leave` are destructive: only run them when the user explicitly requests it, and confirm the exact channel + `ts` first.
- Do not dump raw tokens or full token strings anywhere.

## Output conventions

- Success: a `Success: <method>` line followed by the Slack API response as JSON (IDs like `channel`/`ts`, plus `response_metadata.next_cursor` for paging).
- Failure: a single `Failure: ...` line on stderr with a non-zero exit code. Slack error names (`invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, `rate_limited`, ...) are preserved in the message.
- HTTP 429 and 5xx responses are retried automatically with backoff.

# Slack Web API Reference

Companion reference for the `slack-api` skill. Read this file when you need endpoint details, OAuth scope requirements, or troubleshooting guidance. The helper script `scripts/slack_api.cjs` implements the common operations; use its `api <method> <json>` escape hatch for anything not listed here.

## Contents

1. [Conventions](#conventions)
2. [Authentication and scopes](#authentication-and-scopes)
3. [Endpoints by category](#endpoints-by-category)
4. [Pagination](#pagination)
5. [Rate limits](#rate-limits)
6. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Conventions

- **Base URL**: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`. The script POSTs JSON with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Channel IDs** start with `C` (public channel), `G` (private channel or group DM), `D` (DM). **User IDs** start with `U`, bot IDs with `B`. Prefer IDs in API calls; the script resolves names to IDs when given `#name`.
- **Message timestamps (`ts`)** look like `1699999999.000100`. They are opaque identifiers, not dates: always keep them as strings and never convert to numbers. The `ts` of a parent message also identifies its thread and is passed as `thread_ts` when replying.
- **Text formatting**: messages use Slack mrkdwn: `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, `` ```pre``` ``, `<https://example.com|Link text>`, `<!channel>`, `<@U123>`. Newlines are fine inside the text field.
- **Block Kit**: `chat.postMessage` etc. accept a `blocks` JSON array for rich layouts (headers, sections, buttons, inputs). When sending blocks you can omit `text`, but note some surfaces (e.g. notifications) fall back to `text` if provided, so include a short text fallback for important messages.

## Authentication and scopes

Tokens never expire by themselves but can be revoked. Ask for a token with the minimal scope set for the task. Bot tokens start with `xoxb-`, user tokens with `xoxp-`. OAuth **scopes are per workspace installation**; a bot may have different scopes in different workspaces.

| Operation | Web API method | Typical required scopes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verify token | `auth.test` | none |
| Send / edit / delete messages | `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`, `chat.delete`, `chat.scheduleMessage` | `chat:write` |
| Read public channel history | `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies` | `channels:history` |
| Read private / group DM / DM history | `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies` | `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history` |
| List / inspect channels | `conversations.list`, `conversations.info` | `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read` |
| Create channels | `conversations.create` | `channels:manage` (public), `groups:write` (private) |
| Join channels | `conversations.join` | `channels:join` |
| Leave / rename / set topic | `conversations.leave`, `conversations.rename`, `conversations.setTopic`, `conversations.setPurpose` | `channels:manage`, `groups:write` |
| List / look up users | `users.list`, `users.info`, `users.lookupByEmail` | `users:read` |
| Search messages | `search.messages` | `search:read` |
| Reactions | `reactions.add`, `reactions.remove` | `reactions:write` |
| Upload files | `files.upload` | `files:write` |

When a token is missing a scope, Slack responds `{ "ok": false, "error": "missing_scope", "needed": "chat:write" }` — the `needed` field names the scope to request. The script surfaces it verbatim.

## Endpoints by category

### Messaging
- `chat.postMessage` — body: `{ "channel": "C123", "text": "...", "thread_ts": "optional" }`. Returns `{ "ok": true, "channel": "C123", "ts": "1699999999.000100", "message": {...} }`. The returned `ts` is needed to later update, delete, or react to the message.
- `chat.update` — `{ "channel", "ts", "text" }`; only messages posted by the same bot/user can be edited.
- `chat.delete` — `{ "channel", "ts" }`.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` — like `postMessage` plus `post_at` (Unix time); returns a `scheduled_message_id`. Messages cannot be scheduled more than 120 days out.
- Threads: any message with `thread_ts` set becomes part of the thread of the message with that `ts`. Replies carry a `parent_user_id` and `thread_ts` in responses.

### Conversation content
- `conversations.history` — `{ "channel", "limit", "cursor", "oldest", "latest", "inclusive" }`. `limit` default 100, max 999. `oldest`/`latest` accept Unix timestamps (seconds) or `ts` values; results are newest-first. Messages appear with `user` (author ID), `text`, `ts`, optional `thread_ts`, `reactions`, `files`.
- `conversations.replies` — `{ "channel", "ts" }` fetches the parent message plus all replies in its thread.
- `conversations.list` — `{ "types": "public_channel", "limit": 200, "cursor" }`. `types` is a comma-separated mix of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im`. Set `exclude_archived: true` to skip archived channels.
- `conversations.info` — returns channel metadata: `name`, `topic`, `purpose`, `is_member`, `is_archived`, `num_members`.

### Users
- `users.list` — paginated list; `limit` max 200. Each entry has `id`, `name`, `real_name`, `profile.email`, `profile.display_name`, `is_bot`, `deleted`.
- `users.info` — `{ "user": "U123" }`.
- `users.lookupByEmail` — `{ "email" }`; errors with `users_not_found` when no match.

### Search
- `search.messages` — `{ "query", "count" }`. Query syntax: `from:@alice`, `in:#general`, `after:2024-01-01`, quoted phrases, `is:thread`. Response contains `messages.matches[]` with `channel`/`permalink` context plus paging in `paging`.

### Reactions
- `reactions.add` — `{ "channel", "name": "+1", "timestamp": "1699999999.000100" }`. Emoji names are written without colons (`:+1:` -> `+1`, `:white_check_mark:` -> `white_check_mark`). Custom emoji work by name too.
- `reactions.remove` — same body; errors with `no_reaction` if the emoji is not present.

## Pagination

List and search endpoints paginate with cursors, not offsets:

1. Call with an optional `limit` (e.g. 100).
2. Read `response_metadata.next_cursor` from the result. An empty string means the end.
3. Re-issue the request with `cursor: <next_cursor>` to get the next page.

The script prints a `NOTE: ... --cursor <cursor>` line whenever a next page exists, so follow it iteratively to collect complete results (e.g. a full channel export or full user list).

## Rate limits

Slack rate limits apply per method and are tiered by workspace plan; a typical default is roughly 1 request per second per method, with much higher burst limits on paid plans.

- HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds). The script waits and retries automatically (up to 4 attempts).
- Common causes: tight loops over the same method, or hammering pagination without delay. When iterating pages, respect the response pacing: if you receive a 429, back off at least as long as `Retry-After`.
- Writes (post/update/delete/react) are far less tolerant of bursts than reads. Batch messages with a small delay between sends (e.g. 1s) if posting many at once.

## Troubleshooting

| Slack error | Meaning and fix |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_auth` | Token is wrong or revoked. Ask the user for a valid token. |
| `missing_scope` | Token lacks a permission; `needed` lists it. Ask the user to install the app with that scope (see table above). |
| `not_in_channel` | Bot must join the channel first: run `channel-join <channel>` (or have an admin add it). |
| `channel_not_found` | ID/name is wrong, or the bot cannot see the channel (not a member / not shared). |
| `is_archived` | The channel is archived; it cannot receive messages. |
| `restricted_action` / `enterprise_is_restricted` | Workspace policy blocks the action for this app/user. |
| `invalid_blocks` | The `blocks` JSON does not conform to Block Kit schema. |
| `msg_too_long` | Text exceeds 40,000 characters; split the message. |
| `ratelimited` | Slow down; retry after the delay. |
| `user_not_found` / `users_not_found` | Bad user ID or email. |

General debugging pattern: run `auth-test` first to confirm the token, then the failing call again with `--verbose` to see the raw Slack response, then consult the table.

# Slack API Interaction

## Quick start

- Base URL: `https://slack.com/api`
- Authenticate every request with an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
- Read the token from an environment variable such as `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`; never hardcode or print tokens.
- Send JSON with `Content-Type: application/json` unless an endpoint specifies `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
- Every response is an envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "<code>", ...}`. Always check `ok` before using payload fields; on failure report the `error` code (and `response_metadata` if present) to the user.

Minimal send example:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_BOT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel": "C0123456789", "text": "Hello from Gemini CLI"}'
```

## Message sending and lifecycle

- `chat.postMessage`: send a message. Required: `channel` (channel ID, DM ID, or user ID) and either `text` or `blocks`. Optional useful fields: `thread_ts` (reply in a thread), `reply_broadcast`, `mrkdwn`, `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `link_names`.
- `chat.postEphemeral`: send a message visible only to one `user` in a `channel`.
- `chat.update`: edit a message by `channel` + `ts`.
- `chat.delete`: delete a message by `channel` + `ts`.
- `chat.getPermalink`: get a permanent link for `channel` + `message_ts`.
- `chat.scheduleMessage` / `chat.deleteScheduledMessage`: schedule or cancel a message with a `post_at` Unix timestamp.
- Rich messages: prefer `blocks` (Block Kit JSON) over long `text`. Render user and channel mentions with `<@USERID>` / `<#CHANNELID>`; these are not resolved from display names.
- Returned `ts` values are message IDs and thread timestamps; treat them as opaque strings.

## Conversation and history lookups

Channels, private channels, DMs, and group DMs are all "conversations". Use the `conversations.*` methods:

- `conversations.list`: list conversations. Filter with `types=public_channel,private_channel,im,mpim` (comma-separated) and `exclude_archived=true`. Use the returned `id` as the `channel` value.
- `conversations.history`: fetch recent messages. Params: `channel`, `limit` (1–200, default 100), `cursor`, `oldest`/`latest` (Unix timestamps), `inclusive`, `include_all_metadata`. Returns newest-first messages in `messages[]`.
- `conversations.replies`: get the full thread (`thread_ts` = parent message `ts`) for a message.
- `conversations.info`: get conversation metadata including `is_archived`, `is_private`, `name`, and `last_read`-style markers.
- `conversations.members`: list member user IDs of a conversation (may require `cursor` pagination).
- To find a DM id for a user, use `conversations.open` with `users=<USERID>` (do not hardcode DM ids, they change).
- `conversations.join` / `conversations.leave` / `conversations.archive` for channel membership operations.

## Users

- `users.list`: list workspace users. May return only the first page with `response_metadata.next_cursor`; paginate when present.
- `users.info`: profile by `user` id. Useful fields: `user.real_name`, `user.profile.display_name`, `user.profile.email`, `user.deleted`, `user.is_bot`.
- `users.lookupByEmail`: resolve a user from an email address.
- `users.conversations`: list conversations a user is in (auth token's user) — useful for enumerating accessible channels.

## Reactions, search, files, pins

- `reactions.add`: `{channel, name, timestamp}`. `reactions.remove` removes one; `reactions.get` reads them.
- Search (`search.messages`, `search.files`) requires a user token with `search:read`; bot tokens generally cannot search. When a search call fails with `missing_scope`, explain the token limitation rather than retrying.
- File upload (modern flow): `files.getUploadURLExternal` with `filename` and `length`, then POST the file bytes to the returned `upload_url`, then `files.completeUploadExternal` with the returned `file_id`; optionally pass `channel_id` to share. Legacy `files.upload` still works but is deprecated.
- `pins.add` / `pins.list`: pin or list pinned items in a channel.

## Pagination and rate limits

- Pagination: list-style endpoints return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Repeat the request adding `cursor=<next_cursor>` until it is empty. Prefer `cursor` over `page`/`count`.
- Rate limits: HTTP 429 responses include a `Retry-After` header (seconds). Sleep that long and retry; also honor `X-Slack-Rate-Limit-*` headers and default tier limits by backing off after bursts. For interactive use, space bulk calls out.
- Other common errors to surface: `not_in_channel` (join first), `channel_not_found` (verify the id is a conversation id, not a display name), `invalid_auth` (bad or expired token), `missing_scope` (token lacks a required scope), `is_archived` (channel archived), `ratelimited`.
- Channel/user ids are fixed-prefixed (`C` channels, `D` DMs, `U` users, `W` bot users, `T` teams). Never guess an id; always resolve via the API when unsure.

## Workflow guidance

- Resolve ids before acting: given a channel name or user name/email, first call `conversations.list`/`users.lookupByEmail` to obtain the id, then perform the intended operation.
- Prefer read-only operations when the user asks to inspect; only send, edit, or delete messages when the user clearly requests it. Confirm destructive actions (deletes, message edits) before executing.
- Verify writes: after `chat.postMessage`, surface the returned `ts` and, when asked to confirm delivery, optionally call `conversations.history` to verify.
- Never echo full message bodies of private channels or user tokens into output without need; return trimmed summaries.
- When the Slack API returns a structured error, report `error` plus any `needed`/`provided` scope fields so the user can fix token scopes.
